plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/24562
No template tag on the issue ('Needs Details'); Hacking-ext-unknown inferred: Recruit reports only unauthorized access by a third party to Car Sensor net-related systems, with cause and scope under investigation; no malware, ransomware or extortion reported. Vector Web application / asset S - Web application per the template (affected systems are the Car Sensor net website/app and the C-MATCH dealer web service; the hosting is not described).
Victim: Recruit Co., Ltd. (Car Sensor net used-car listings, C-MATCH dealer support). NAICS changed from 5112 (software publishers) to 519130 (Internet Publishing and Broadcasting and Web Search Portals) because Car Sensor is an online listing/classifieds service. Employee count 10001 to 25000 is approximate and not confirmed against a fetched source in this pass (web lookups were rate-limited); please verify.
Data (maximum counts that 'may have been leaked', total 3,709,551): Car Sensor inquiry users 3,210,421 (names, addresses - 447,670 with street-level address - inquiry content, age range, gender, some phone/fax/email); review posters 5,289; C-MATCH registered used-car dealers 483,168 (contact names, phones, used-goods dealer licence numbers, login IDs; sole proprietors may include business address and direct-debit account information -> Bank); Recruit employees/former staff and outsourced/sales agency staff 10,673 (names, emails, login IDs). No card data or login passwords, so Credentials not coded. data_victim Customer, Partner (dealers), Employee. data_disclosure Potentially: Recruit gives 'maximum' counts that may have been leaked and has not confirmed exfiltration.
Timeline: suspicious external access detected Oct 17, 2026; services suspended ~17:00 that day; scope identified Oct 20; disclosed Oct 21 with preliminary PPC report. Access start date unknown, so incident coded 2026-10 and discovery duration Unknown. Discovery internal (Recruit detected the access; how not stated) -> internal Unknown. dbir_year 2027.
A kumanichi headline seen in search ('Carsensor info leak; Nissan and Mitsubishi Motors also halt used-car sites') suggests other carmakers' used-car sites were suspended; Impress (Car Watch) names no other affected company, and that article could not be read, so no secondary victims are coded - reviewer may wish to check whether a shared platform was involved.
Sources: Bernama (issue) gives only the 3.7M figure; details from Car Watch (Impress). Confidence Medium: action unknown and exfiltration unconfirmed.

event_chain.summary: Unauthorized access to Car Sensor systems; data taken

summary: Recruit Co. detected suspicious external access to systems behind its Car Sensor net used-car listing service on October 17, 2026 and suspended Car Sensor net, its app and the C-MATCH dealer service. On October 21 it disclosed that personal data for up to 3,709,551 people may have been leaked: Car Sensor inquiry users and review posters (names, addresses, some contact details), 483,168 used-car dealers registered with C-MATCH (contact details, dealer licence numbers, login IDs and, for some sole proprietors, direct-debit account data) and 10,673 Recruit employees and contractor staff. No card data or login passwords were involved.
